rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: CAA passenger and crew power-bank rule changes took effect on 27 March 2026.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: The updated restrictions aim to reduce the likelihood and impact of lithium-battery thermal events.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: Spare lithium batteries and power banks must be individually protected against short circuits when not in use.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: Battery-powered devices must be protected from accidental activation.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: Relevant batteries must meet UN Manual of Tests and Criteria Part III section 38.3.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: Standard limits include 2 grams lithium content for lithium-metal batteries and 100 Wh for lithium-ion batteries.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: Power banks must be carried in carry-on baggage rather than checked baggage.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: Power banks must not be recharged onboard and the amended rule allows a maximum of two per person.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: Lithium-battery flight risk depends on chemistry, rating, manufacture, condition, damage, packing, terminal protection, baggage location, use and operator approval.

rows.source: CAA lithium-battery and power-bank flight safety
rows.verified: CAA battery evidence is battery-, device-, passenger-, baggage-, operator-, flight- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: ORR guidance provides a structured approach for rail companies to manage fatigue risk.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: The revised approach uses a Plan, Do, Check, Act management cycle.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: ORR defines fatigue as reduced mental or physical capability linked to sleep loss, extended wakefulness, circadian disruption, workload or prolonged work.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: Fatigue can reduce alertness, slow reactions and impair decision making.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: Performance effects include reduced vigilance, awareness, tracking ability and memory.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: Contributing factors include roster timing, duty length, consecutive duties, workload, sleep quality and the work environment.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: Employers should manage work-related factors and staff should report fatigue concerns and obtain sufficient sleep.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: The guidance is directed to those managing railway staff, including controllers of safety-critical work under regulation 25 of ROGS.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: Rail-fatigue risk depends on roster design, sleep, circadian timing, workload, travel, recovery, individual health, reporting culture and task criticality.

rows.source: ORR rail-staff fatigue management
rows.verified: ORR fatigue evidence is worker-, roster-, task-, operator-, route-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
